references.text: Luke 20:43 is a direct quote from [ref:Ps 110:1|Psalm 110:1], where the Lord says to David's Lord: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet." Jesus quotes this psalm to show that the Messiah is more than just David's son – he is also David's Lord.

Peter quotes the same passage from [ref:Acts 2:34-35|Acts of the Apostles 2:34-35] in his Pentecost sermon, applying Psalm 110:1 to Jesus Christ and his exaltation at God's right hand: "until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."

[ref:Heb 1:13|The Epistle to the Hebrews 1:13] also quotes Psalm 110:1 and applies it to Christ to demonstrate his superiority over angels: "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."

[ref:Heb 10:12-13|The Epistle to the Hebrews 10:12-13] alludes to Psalm 110:1 and describes how Christ sat down at God's right hand after offering a single sacrifice for sins, and now waits until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.

[ref:1 Cor 15:25|1 Corinthians 15:25] states that Christ will reign "until God has put all enemies under his feet", reflecting the same theme from Psalm 110:1 concerning the Messiah's dominion over his foes.
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:44|Matthew 22:44] presents the same quote from Psalm 110:1 during Jesus' discussion with the Pharisees about who the Messiah is.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:36|Mark 12:36] contains the same quote from Psalm 110:1, where Jesus asks how David can call the Messiah "Lord" when he is his son.
